Phase 2 · Portfolio management and stress testing

Build the portfolio, then try to break it

Integrate approved securities, test the whole IPS, apply the committee's bear case, and revise any portfolio that cannot meet the client mandate.

Inputs, not suggestions

Carry forward the approved mandate and security decisions

No candidate security or portfolio weight may be approved unless the team identifies the Phase 1 client need, constraint, unresolved question, or downstream guardrail it addresses.

  1. Approved client objective and RRTTLLU constraints
  2. Required and desired return, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire
  3. Liquidity dates, cash-flow needs, tax considerations, values, and unique constraints
  4. Committee base and bear macro scenarios with source dates
  5. Phase 1 Analyst Decision Log, including unresolved information gaps and downstream guardrails

Scenario integrity rule

The bear case must use the Phase 1 assumptions the committee approved. Do not soften a return, volatility, rate, spread, or correlation assumption merely to make the portfolio pass.

Portfolio workflow

Allocate, test, correct, and vote

1

Assemble

Place approved securities into sleeves and assign tentative weights. State the job of every sleeve and holding.

2

Reconcile

Check that weights total 100%, resources match the hypothetical AUM, and every holding traces to a Phase 1 guardrail and a verified selection decision.

3

Measure

Calculate expected return and required course risk measures consistently; identify concentration, overlap, duration, credit, liquidity, and benchmark/style exposures.

4

Test the IPS

Compare the integrated portfolio with every client objective, constraint, limit, and tripwire—not only the return target.

5

Run the bear case

Apply the approved Phase 1 bear assumptions without softening them, quantify portfolio and dollar impacts, and explain which client goal is most exposed.

6

Correct and re-test

For every breach, record specific trades or constraint changes, explain the trade-off, recalculate the full portfolio, and confirm whether the revised portfolio passes.

7

Vote

Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. Record dissent, monitoring triggers, and action owners.

Bear-case template

Quantify the downside and the client consequence

Bear-case stress template. Apply the approved Phase 1 assumptions and show both percentage and dollar impacts.
Scenario variable or asset classPhase 1 bear assumption and sourcePortfolio exposure / weightEstimated return or value impactDollar impactIPS limit or client goal testedPass / warning / breachEvidence, limitation, or assumption

Interpret before correcting

Name the exposure that causes the loss, the client goal or constraint placed at risk, the limits of the estimate, and whether the result is a pass, warning, or breach.

FactSet input record

For each FactSet-derived return, risk, exposure, correlation, or benchmark input, record what was retrieved, the retrieval date, definition and units, as-of period, source reference as appropriate, limitation, and effect on the portfolio decision. Submit the required licensed evidence privately through Canvas; do not place proprietary exports or student work in the public repository.

Document the adjustment and re-test

Breach and root cause

No breach is cured by narrative. Record the actual trade or approved constraint change, calculate the revised portfolio, identify the new trade-off, and run the IPS and bear-case tests again.

Four-person ownership

Risk belongs to the entire committee

Owned work

Client and Macro Strategist

Confirm that the integrated allocation still serves the client's ranked goals and all RRTTLLU constraints.

Owned work

Fixed-Income Analyst

Explain how the fixed-income sleeve changes income reliability, rate sensitivity, credit risk, liquidity, and bear-case protection.

Owned work

Fund and ETF Analyst

Test whether pooled vehicles deliver the intended exposure and diversification without hidden duplication or avoidable cost.

Owned work

Portfolio Manager and Risk Analyst

Own integration, calculation checks, IPS scorecard, bear-case test, breach escalation, corrections, re-test, and the committee vote record.

Portfolio approval gate

Approve only a traceable, tested recommendation

  • Every holding has a verified selection record, a portfolio job, an accountable role owner, and a Phase 1 guardrail reference.
  • Weights total 100% and dollar allocations reconcile to the hypothetical AUM.
  • Return and risk calculations use consistent as-of dates, units, and scenario assumptions.
  • The IPS scorecard tests all relevant objectives and constraints; the team does not declare compliance from one metric.
  • The bear case exactly carries forward the approved Phase 1 assumptions and shows both percentage and dollar impact.
  • Every warning or breach has a documented decision; every breach is corrected and re-tested before approval.
  • The final portfolio states monitoring triggers, remaining uncertainties, and what would cause the committee to reconvene.

AI boundary

AI may challenge assumptions, suggest a counter-scenario, or help debug a formula. The team must verify every factual or numerical claim, run its own calculations, and own the final allocation, correction, and vote.

Complete the decision package

Attach the final IPS scorecard, bear-case result, correction and re-test if needed, all four votes, dissent or reservations, and monitoring triggers.
